cognate: Arm. anown = Ved. nā́man- < *h₁nómn̥; Arm. dnem (aor. ed-) = Ved. dhā- < *dʰeh₁- 'put'
shared_syntax: name + 'put' as the act of naming, with the name actually given as predicate (Arm. Դրունս Փոսից; Ved. dán apástamaḥ). In RV 10.115.2a nā́ma is probably adverbial ('Agni by name has been set as most active biter'), so the slab anchor shows nā́ma + dhā- in a naming statement rather than the transitive idiom itself; the transitive idiom proper is in the support lines (RV 1.72.3c nā́māni dadhire, Od. 19.406 τίθεσθ̓ ὄνομ̓, Faustos dnel anown).
context: Both are naming acts: Agathangelos names a frontier place ('put the name Gates of the Pits on the place'); RV 10.115.2 says Agni 'has been put as name' most active biter. The pairing name + 'put' (not 'call', 'give') is the idiom of naming in both; Faustos uses the same Armenian idiom for naming a founded estate, Homer has ὄνομα τίθεσθαι for naming a child, the RV nā́ma dhā- repeatedly. Recalled: Hitt. lāman dai- and Lat. nōmen indere complete the set (*h₁nómn̥ dʰeh₁-) in the handbooks. Caveat: Christian Armenian could calque Gk ὄνομα τιθέναι (Gen. 2), so the Armenian testimony alone is not decisive. Note for review: BS-88457 was not among my flagged bundles; the RV 10.115.2a anchor was found by searching my own slab for name + 'put'.

words.etymon: derḱ- (slab and lexicon mapping; standard but debated)

cognate: Arm. keam = Lat. uīta (and Gk ζώω, support) < *gʷ(y)eh₃- 'live'; Arm. loys = Lat. lūmen < *lewk- 'light'; if the standard derivation of Arm. tesanem from *derḱ- is accepted, Arm. tesanel = Ved. dṛśé is a third cognate pair
drift_or_renewal: object renewed: 'sun' (Ved. sū́rya-, Gk ἠέλιος) vs 'light' (Arm. loys, Gk φάος, Lat. lūmen); verb 'see': Arm. tesanem ~ Ved. dṛś- (*derḱ-, debated), Gk ὁράω renewed
shared_syntax: 'live' coordinated with or glossed by 'see the light/sun' (Arm. keal ew zloys tesanel 'to live and see the light'; Gk ζώει καὶ ὁρᾷ φάος ἠελίοιο; Ved. jyók sū́ryaṃ dṛśé 'long to see the sun' = long life; Lat. lūmina vītae)
context: Agathangelos: the king's man says Gregory 'does not want to live and see the light', i.e. to stay alive; exactly the Homeric 'lives and sees the light of the sun' (Il. 18.61), with Arm. keam cognate with ζώω. The Armenian idiom is not only Christian: in the Artawazd curse that Movses Khorenacʻi quotes from the old songs, 'may you not see the light' means 'may you die'. AVŚ 12.2.36 carries the Vedic wish to 'see the sun long'; Lucretius' lumina vitae joins the same two Latin roots (*lewk- and *gʷeyh₃-) as the Armenian. Recalled: 'to see the light of the sun' = 'to be alive' is in the handbooks as an inherited figure (Ved., Gk., also elsewhere). Caveats: the image is natural, and biblical 'see light' could have reinforced the Armenian; the Armenian object (light) is not cognate with the Vedic (sun), and the tesanem < *derḱ- derivation is debated.
phrase: 'live and see the light (of the sun)' = to be alive
